# Redaction policy v1

<!-- Generated by gramps/redaction/render_reference.py from gramps/redaction/redaction-v1.json. Do not edit by hand: change the JSON, regenerate, and commit both. -->

What never goes to the cloud, as one declarative rule file. This page is generated from `gramps/redaction/redaction-v1.json`; a unit test fails when the two differ. Rationale for the privacy model is in [The privacy model for family data](../explanation/family-data-privacy.md).

Basis: sync.md section 5, as amended by BRD2 section 11.1; BRD2 D2-32, Q2-02 and Q2-18; review findings PS-01, PS-02, PS-03, PS-06, PS-15, SI-16 and SI-19.

## Where the policy lives

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `gramps/redaction/redaction-v1.json` | The rules, the birth-like list and the tables below. The only source. |
| `gramps/redaction/redaction-v1.schema.json` | The JSON Schema the file validates against. |
| `gramps/redaction/vectors/*.json` | Golden vectors: input objects, the expected projection, the expected holds and the server validator's verdict. Python and JavaScript both pass them. |
| `gramps/redaction/make_vectors.py` | Generates the vectors; `--check` compares bytes. |
| `gramps/hfygramps/rules.py` | The Python loader and the pure predicates, `is_birth_like` first. |
| `shared/redaction-rules.mjs` | The JavaScript port of the same predicates; it takes the parsed policy as an argument. |
| `gramps/tests/unit/redaction_oracle.py` | Test-only reference reading of the rules that the vectors are checked against. It is not the projection or the validator. |

The projection, the server validator, the edit guard and the renderer are to import this one file and keep no list of their own (D2-32).

## Order of application

The projection `P(tree)` is a pure function of the whole local tree. Each rule names the phase it belongs to.

1. **classify.** Decide which primary objects are excluded or held, from their own flags, types and files. No other object is needed.
2. **elements.** Remove private secondary elements from each kept object.
3. **fields.** Reduce dates, blank local-only fields and round coordinates on each kept object.
4. **scan.** Scan the outgoing free text. A hit holds a field of an object the cloud already has, or the whole object when it is new.
5. **orphans.** Exclude, until nothing more changes, every object that only excluded or held objects reference.
6. **references.** Filter references to excluded or held objects, and re-point places.

## Birth-like events

The one list of birth-like events. The projection, the server validator, the edit guard and the renderer import this predicate; nobody keeps a local list (D2-32).

An event is birth-like when any of these holds, for everyone, living or deceased:

- Its type is one of: Birth 12, Adult Christening 14, Baptism 15, Bless 18, Christen 22, Stillbirth 45.
- Its type is Custom (0) and the type name matches `/birth|bapt|christen|naissance|geburt|nacimiento/i` (a substring match; ASCII case folding only).
- Some person references it at its `birth_ref_index`, whatever its type.

Day and month mean `dateval` indexes 0, 1, 4, 5. A date of a birth-like event is reduced to:

- Those indexes set to 0, in both halves of a RANGE or SPAN; the years (indexes 2, 6), the slash flags, the modifier, the quality, the calendar and the new-year flag unchanged.
- `text` set to the empty string. The server accepts only a bare year (`^[0-9]{1,4}$`) or nothing.
- A TEXTONLY date (modifier 6) becomes a plain date with the first four-digit year of its text (`(?:^|[^0-9])([0-9]{4})(?![0-9])`, group 1), or an empty date when the text has none.
- `sortval` recomputed as the day number of January 1 of the year in the date's calendar, for the calendars 0, 1 (Gregorian 0, Julian 1), and 0 when the year is 0 or the calendar is another.

A name of type Birth (name type 2) and a citation referenced by a birth-like event or by its EventRef are reduced the same way.

## Rules

Each rule has an id, a class, the Gramps classes it applies to, a path pattern, an action and a phase. Path patterns are RFC 6901 pointers in which `*` is one key or list index, `**` is any depth (including none) and `{a,b}` lists alternatives. `server` says whether the server validator detects a violation of the rule (`detect`) or cannot (`none`: it needs local data, bytes or the whole local tree). A rule marked desktop-only needs data the cloud never holds.

### Actions

- `exclude_object`: The whole object stays out of the cloud (or is held).
- `filter_element`: An element or a reference is removed from its list, or a handle is nulled.
- `hold_media`: A Media object stays out of the cloud until io releases it.
- `local_only`: A field or element stays on the desktop; the cloud gets the empty value.
- `reduce_date`: A Date loses day, month and text and keeps its year.
- `repoint_place`: A reference to an excluded place moves to the nearest kept ancestor.
- `round_coordinates`: A coordinate is rounded to the policy's decimals.
- `scan`: A hit of the shared detector in an outgoing text field holds the field, or the whole object when it is new.

## Tables the rules read

### Attributes

- Local-only age and time attributes: Age 10, Father Age 11, Mother Age 12, Time 14.
- Local-only government identifiers: Social Security Number 6, Identification Number 3.

### Contact URLs

- URL type 1 (Email) is local-only.
- Schemes: `mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`, `callto:`, `facetime:`, `skype:`, `whatsapp:`.
- Hosts, matched by registrable-domain suffix and never by substring: `m.me`, `ig.me`, `wa.me`, `t.me`, `telegram.me`, `messenger.com`, `api.whatsapp.com`, `signal.me`.
- Paths: `instagram.com/m/`.

### Places

- Excluded by type: Street 7, Farm 18, Building 19, Number 20.
- Excluded when the type is Custom (0) and its name matches `/house|home|residence|address|apartment|apt|lot|farm/i`. This is a substring match, so a name that merely contains one of the words is excluded too.
- A place code stays only for: Country 1, State 2, County 3, Province 8, Region 9, Department 10. Every other type keeps it local.
- Alternate-location fields blanked: `street`, `locality`, `postal`, `phone`.
- Coordinates: a plain decimal (`^[+-]?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$`) is rounded half away from zero to 2 decimals, and a value with no more decimals keeps its text; anything else is blanked.

### Media

- Held until io releases them, by mime type: `application/pdf`.
- Held when the file has EXIF GPS latitude or longitude, by mime type: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/tiff`.
- A media reference rectangle is four integers from 0 to 100 with x1 < x2 and y1 < y2. `[0, 0, 100, 100]` is normalised to null; any other shape is held.

### Free-text scan

- Detector kinds (the one R-18 detector, `shared/privacy-guard.mjs` and `gramps/hfygramps/scanner.py`): `phone`, `email`, `street_address`, `po_box`, `contact_url`, `dob_heuristic`.
- Desktop-only kinds: `dob_exact`. The window for a birth keyword or a name is 60 characters.
- A hit on an existing synced object keeps the last synced value of that field; a hit on a new object holds the whole object, and references to it are filtered. A styled note is one atomic field: holding it keeps the base tags too.

## Readings this file records

The design leaves these open; the file fixes them, and each is raised for confirmation.

- `private.citation.source_excluded`: A Citation whose Source is excluded or held is excluded too, repeatedly with private.orphan.exclude: a citation cannot exist without its source. This task's reading of sync.md 5.1, which lists no filter for source_handle.
- `private.reference.event_place`: An event place that is private or held is set to the empty string. This task's reading: the design lists placeref_list but not Event.place, and a private place must not be named by an event.

## Vectors

`gramps/redaction/vectors/<group>.json` holds `{policy, group, vectors}`. A vector is `{id, title, rules, context, input, expected}`:

- `input` is a list of partial Gramps `json_data` objects; every nested element carries its `_class`, and a missing key means the Gramps default.
- `context` may hold `base` (the last synced projected object per handle), `files` (per media handle: `exif_gps`, `md5`, `readable`), `released` (media handles io released) and `sticky` (event handles that were ever birth-like).
- `expected.projection` maps every input handle to the projected object, or to `null` when it is excluded or held and never synced. `expected.excluded` lists `{handle, rule}`; `expected.holds` lists `{handle, rule, scope, pointer}` with scope `object` or `field`.
- `expected.server` is the server validator's verdict on `input` as submitted: `{ok, violations: [{rule, handle, pointer}]}`, pointers per RFC 6901. The projection of every input must itself pass.
- `expected.birth_like`, when present, lists the events `isBirthLike` must accept.
- `rules` names the rule ids the vector exercises. Every rule id is named by at least one vector.

Regenerate and check:

```bash
python3 gramps/redaction/make_vectors.py            # rewrite the vectors
python3 gramps/redaction/render_reference.py        # rewrite this page
python3 -m unittest discover gramps/tests/unit      # the checks, including both drift tests
cd api && npx vitest run test/redaction-rules.test.js   # the JavaScript port against the same vectors
```

## Not in this file

- Non-birth dates are stored at full precision and published as years only; that is the renderer's rule (Q2-04b), not part of the projection.
- The scan of members' posts, comments and chat is the shared detector (`shared/privacy-guard.mjs`), not a rule here.
- The merge, lift and conflict rules (sync.md section 6) read this policy but do not live in it.
